players.product: AI data-center colocation (Tydal, Norway: 121 IT MW leased to Volta for NVIDIA GPUs) and Bitdeer AI GPU cloud (NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 / Vera Rubin capacity in Malaysia, Norway and the US)

quarterly_data.signal: Power infrastructure summary as of July 31, 2026 (Q2 2026 results release): Knoxville, Tennessee (86 MW, crypto to AI cloud) - to meet customer demand for larger scale deployments, the project was fully redesigned, with overall completion now targeted for Q3 2027 (Q3 '27); Wenatchee, Washington (13 MW, crypto to AI cloud) - ready-for-service timing to be updated, the mining datacenter has been removed and Bitdeer plans to change the design to accommodate the latest NVIDIA GPUs; Tydal, Norway colocation in three phases - 66.5 MW Q4 2026, 66.5 MW Q1 2027 and 47 MW H2 2027 (two additional data halls for future AI / HPC use cases); Fox Creek, Alberta energization now expected for Q4 2027. Online electrical capacity 1,752 MW; total global electrical capacity 2,980.2 MW.
quarterly_data.figure: Knoxville 86 MW AI conversion redesigned, completion Q3 2027; Tydal 66.5 MW + 66.5 MW + 47 MW; 2,980.2 MW total

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 business-line detail (results release): AI Cloud revenue US$14.0 million, cost of revenue US$16.3 million, gross loss US$2.3 million (Q2 2025: revenue US$1.3 million, gross loss US$0.7 million). Q2 capital expenditures US$266.0 million, of which US$150.0 million was for the production of SEALMINERs used for self-mining and co-mining and US$116.0 million for datacenter infrastructure construction, GPU equipment procurement and tariffs and freight for mining rigs delivered to the datacenters.
quarterly_data.figure: AI Cloud Q2 gross loss US$2.3 million on US$14.0 million revenue; Q2 capex US$266.0 million (US$116.0 million datacenter / GPU)
